freecad_python:
import FreeCAD
import Part
import math

# Reference the starting F0 shape
_ = f0_shape

# Refined L03 forearm link
# Overall envelope based on F0 bbox: 126 x 34 x 32 mm
# J03 hub at x~100, J02 hub at x~13 (spanning ~100mm between joint centers)

# Main body - rectangular bar (load path between joints)
body_len = 100.0
body_w = 18.0
body_h = 22.0
body = Part.makeBox(body_len, body_w, body_h)
body.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(13.0, -9.0, -11.0))

# Hub at J03 end (wrist side, x=100) - larger ring for joint bearing
hub1_outer_r = 17.0
hub1_inner_r = 8.0
hub1_h = 34.0
hub1_outer = Part.makeCylinder(hub1_outer_r, hub1_h)
hub1_outer.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(100.0, 0.0, -hub1_h/2.0))
hub1_inner = Part.makeCylinder(hub1_inner_r, hub1_h)
hub1_inner.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(100.0, 0.0, -hub1_h/2.0))
hub1 = hub1_outer.cut(hub1_inner)

# Hub at J02 end (elbow side, x=13) - smaller ring for joint bearing
hub2_outer_r = 13.0
hub2_inner_r = 6.0
hub2_h = 34.0
hub2_outer = Part.makeCylinder(hub2_outer_r, hub2_h)
hub2_outer.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(13.0, 0.0, -hub2_h/2.0))
hub2_inner = Part.makeCylinder(hub2_inner_r, hub2_h)
hub2_inner.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(13.0, 0.0, -hub2_h/2.0))
hub2 = hub2_outer.cut(hub2_inner)

# Fuse all components into single solid
result = body.fuse(hub1)
result = result.fuse(hub2)

result_shape = result
assumptions: Joint hub centers are positioned at approximately x=13 (J02 side) and x=100 (J03 side) in L03 local frame, spanning the ~100mm link length.
Hub outer radii of 17mm (J03) and 13mm (J02) reflect the larger wrist joint housing vs smaller elbow connection visible in F0 renders.
Inner hole radii (8mm and 6mm) represent bearing clearance zones; actual bearing geometry is out of scope.
Main body cross-section of 18×22mm provides structural load path between joints while staying within the 34×32mm bbox envelope.
The link is symmetric about the XZ plane (y=0), consistent with the F0 renders showing bilateral symmetry.
